reason:
The from-rest full stage spends its first 2.0 s in phase=0, where the correction gate
4*phase*(1-phase) is exactly 0: the frozen public acceleration expert runs and NOTHING is
learnable. That prefix was 2.00 s of a 5.73 s mean episode, i.e. 35% of every episode with
zero learnable authority, and the task's own physics says it cannot be improved there: with
the phase=0 window stretched to 8 s the frozen expert still plateaus at .382 m/s, and the
measured velocity plateau is t=2.6-3.4 s at .37-.38 m/s, so the existing handoff at t=3.0 s
already leaves at 95% of that peak and delaying it is worse (0.317 m/s at t=5.0 s). The user
asked to train the glide from speed instead of replaying the push every episode. The assisted
mechanics for that already exist (near/unload/transfer-near/transfer spawn at a measured pose
with an injected speed and phase_start) but every assisted stage capped its injected speed at
.25-.35 m/s and none of them started inside the sustained hold, so there was no stage that
trained the glide itself at the speed the glide actually needs.
change:
Add an assisted glide stage that spawns inside the measured single-support glide and trains the
sustained 2.0 s objective directly. The spawn is MEASURED, not chosen: local/measure-glide-pose.py
rolls out the full stage and records the servo configuration, the servo joint velocities and the
root orientation at the first frame where loaded left-only support holds (63/64 episodes
captured), and local/add-glide-pose.py takes the medians, clamps the positions 1e-4 rad inside the
model's joint ranges, and grounds them on the tyre MESH vertices (the convention
tests/test_onefoot_curriculum.py already enforces). The recorded state is genuinely single
support: the support skate is grounded while the swing skate is clear by 0.0155/0.0727 m, the
entry speed is p50 .505 / p90 .548 / max .585, the median |servo joint velocity| is 1.86 rad/s
with the swing hip at 7.64 rad/s, and the root is pitched 0.106 rad forward. speed_range is
(.45,.58); phase_start=1.0 with acceleration_s=0 and lift_s=1.0 puts phase at exactly 1.0 from
the first control step, so no episode replays the frozen phase=0 prefix; goal_s is 2.0, identical
to full, and episode_length_s is 3.4 s. SUSTAINED_STAGES=('glide','full') makes both stages
certify against the 2.0 s credible metric, and bridge_stage_gate now reads that tuple from the cfg
instead of hardcoding 'full'. The faithful spawn lives in this env-cfg module rather than in
mdp.py deliberately: mdp.py's pre-v15 region is pinned byte-for-byte by
tests/test_old_mdp_and_registry_bytes_are_preserved, and inserting optional parameters into the
shared reset helper would shift that region and destroy an invariant that can never be restored.
reset_credit_bridge_spawn reproduces the shared helper exactly, adding only root_pitch and
joint_vel, and it is installed ONLY for poses that actually carry those extra measured fields, so
every other assisted stage keeps mdp.reset_curriculum_onefoot byte for byte. Spawning the glide
entry without them is not neutral: with the posture of one instant and the joints of a standstill
the same policy's credible 0.5 s rate collapsed from 0.97 to 0.30, because that combined state
never occurs in a real trajectory. glide is an ASSISTED start and is labelled as such by the
existing initial_assistance=(stage!='full') contract, so it can never be presented as from-rest
evidence: only full (HOME, exact zero velocity) certifies a from-rest result. Everything happens
once, at reset; nothing is corrected mid-episode. Two audit gaps are closed as well:
microduck_onefoot_credit_bridge_env_cfg.py and microduck_onefoot_curriculum_poses.py are now both
in COMPATIBLE_SOURCES, so the task timing, the stage definitions and the spawn poses are pinned to
the source run like the reward and the actor. The new named kind task_contract_transition records
this change; its owner file must move, and a transition that is not an actor-forward transition
may never move the actor.
